numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Rolling cov/corr over a series with a large shared offset returns inaccurate values. For the PR#66678 reproducer, the outputs at indices 4:7 are about 1.099968, -0.300072, -0.800026. Windows after a large value leaves the window are silently wrong, and can be NaN once a negative ssqdm_x reaches the square root in calc_corr.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The exact rolling cov values [1.1, -0.3, -0.8] for indices 4:7 of the reproducer.
trigger_conditions: Series carry a large shared offset (x and y are each shifted by 1e12 in the reproducer)
A large value dominating ssqdm_x/ssqdm_y leaves the rolling window, so the accumulators collapse to round-off
Error introduced by an earlier incremental update is not detected one step later by the cancellation test
Rolling window of size 5 with cov computed against another series

numerical_characteristics.precision: rtol=1e-12 used in the test assertion; the incremental update is designed to hold to an rtol tolerance, not float64 noise; InvCondTol = EpsF64 * 1e3 is the cancellation threshold
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Large shared offset of 1e12 added to series values (PR#66678 reproducer); outlier values 1e12 and 1e7 leaving the window; anchor re-centering skipped for values whose magnitude exceeds sqrt(float64 max)
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: rtol=1e-12, atol=0 in the cov/corr test; InvCondTol = EpsF64 * 1e3 for the cancellation check; PR reproducer exact values [1.1, -0.3, -0.8] with wrong outputs near 1.099968, -0.300072, -0.800026
category_specific_evidence: Commit GH#65739: incremental rolling cov/corr accumulators wrong after a large value leaves the window; windows become silently wrong or NaN when negative ssqdm_x reaches sqrt in calc_corr
PR#66678 reproducer: rolling(5).cov on series offset by 1e12 gives values differing from exact [1.1, -0.3, -0.8] at roughly the 1e-4 relative level
Test test_rolling_cov_corr_outlier_exit_no_nan uses window=3 with series containing 1e12, 1e7, -1e12 and asserts no NaN after warm-up, comparing against np.cov/np.corrcoef on recentred chunks
Fix anchors accumulators to first value in window so common offset cancels; MaxOriginMagnitude = sqrt(float64 max) bounds the anchor
Fix tracks peak deviation per accumulator since last recompute and uses cancellation_suspected test on ssqdm_xy, ssqdm_x, ssqdm_y with peak_dev scaling (eps * peak_dev squared)
Test comment states rtol is the tolerance the incremental update is designed to hold to, not float64 noise
reproduction_risks: Test comment says some windows still contain 1e12 so the expected rtol is a design tolerance rather than machine precision; exact outputs in the PR reproducer are printed only to a truncated number of digits
Recompute path (requires_recompute or numerically_unstable) and cancellation thresholds determine which windows are exercised; reproduction depends on window ordering of large-value entry and exit
Negative ssqdm_x from cancellation is the trigger for NaN; reproduction must cover windows after the large value exits
